sources.label: CSS Overflow Module Level 3 text-overflow propdef (editor's draft)

inputs.rationale: This change adds no property and no API surface: the page states there is no new CSS property or JavaScript API, so there are no programmatic inputs to document; the trigger is user interaction, which the #the-behavior table enumerates instead.

outputs.rationale: The feature has no return value: its observable effect is a rendering change on an existing value (text-overflow: ellipsis), described in the #the-behavior table rather than returned to script.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path: the interaction is a rendering behaviour with no throwing surface, and no failure mode is listed in the #the-behavior table.

lifecycle.rationale: There is nothing to construct or tear down in script: the page frames the change as purely in the rendering model, so no lifecycle or cleanup surface exists beyond the browser's own layout cycle.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy surface: #why describes only revealing text that is already in the DOM, on a user gesture (contenteditable titles, filenames, inline-editing widgets), and the ChromeStatus record 5146265241387008 carries no security or privacy considerations.

notes: Pilot unit of campaign B1 (gendn-xpz): the page carried zero id attributes, so the schema could not resolve a single selector to it; six existing section headings gained ids (on the <h2>, because fragmentAfterId() slices to the next <h1-3>) and nothing else in the page changed. SOURCES RE-FETCHED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-06): the W3C css-overflow-3 #ellipsis-interaction fragment is live and its text is 'user interaction with ellipsis - When the user is interacting with content (e.g. editing, selecting, scrolling), the user agent may treat text-overflow: ellipsis as text-overflow: clip'; chromestatus feature 5146265241387008 is 'Clip Text overflow on user interaction' and its record carries the same chromium bug this page cites (40731275), so the record is this feature. CARRIED DISAGREEMENT, BOTH SIDES, NEITHER ADJUDICATED: the page's #browser-support table reads 'Chrome 147 - In developer trial (behind a flag)', while the live ChromeStatus record reads status 'Proposed', desktop/android/webview 149, flag false, origintrial false (created 2026-01-20, updated 2026-04-27). A developer trial riding the generic experimental flag is consistent with flag:false, so the two can coexist as DevTrial-now / ship-target-149; what the page does NOT do is disclose the source's current status.
